title: DHS Announces ICE Body Camera Rollout for All Field Officers by End of September
excerpt: Secretary Mullin announced that all ICE field officers would be equipped with body-worn cameras by the end of September 2026, following a series of deadly and disputed shootings in which agents were not wearing cameras. The announcement came after Congress allocated $20 million specifically for body cameras.
content:
On September 1, 2026, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced at a press conference in New York that Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers in the field were expected to have body-worn cameras by the end of September.

  • DHS awarded two contracts to Axon Enterprise totaling more than $30 million for cameras, and every ICE field office reportedly had enough devices for all officers making arrests by the end of August.
  • ICE had previously predicted full implementation by September 2025 — a deadline missed by a full year. Officials in February 2026 had told lawmakers ICE had only 3,000 cameras for 13,000 officers.
  • The announcement came after two fatal July 2026 shootings — in Houston and Maine — in which neither the target nor the involved ICE officers wore body cameras, prompting bipartisan calls for mandatory camera use.
  • Congress provided $20 million specifically for body cameras but was unable to negotiate a mandate for ICE to purchase or use them.
  • Independent Sen. Angus King of Maine called the rollout announcement a "hollow promise," citing the agency's policy giving the director discretion over releasing footage publicly.

Despite having cameras distributed to field offices, training on how to activate and wear the devices remained incomplete as of the announcement date, raising questions about enforcement of the policy.
